54968.summary: The class explores the names and titles of Jesus Christ to build a personal relationship with him, focusing on understanding their roles and functions in the Bible and how they reflect his identity and purpose. The class also emphasizes the importance of knowing and calling on his name for salvation and a deeper relationship with God.

54969.summary: The class explores the title 'Lord' as applied to Jesus Christ, emphasizing the relationship between lordship and servanthood. It examines biblical passages that illustrate this dynamic, including the parables of the talents and the wise and faithful servant, and highlights the importance of faithfulness and obedience in fulfilling Christ's commands.

54970.summary: The class explores the name and identity of Jesus Christ, emphasizing the importance of building a personal relationship with him through understanding his titles and actions. It discusses the significance of the name Jesus and its role in salvation, highlighting Jesus as a teacher, healer, and savior who overcomes temptation and helps believers overcome their struggles.

54971.summary: The class explores the title 'Christ' as it relates to Jesus, focusing on the Old Testament concept of anointing and its role in sanctifying kings and priests. It emphasizes Jesus as the fulfillment of the Messiah, combining the roles of king and priest, and highlights the significance of his crucifixion and resurrection in providing atonement and salvation.

54972.summary: The class focuses on Jesus Christ as the Master and Teacher, emphasizing His role in teaching and preaching the gospel. It highlights the importance of understanding and following His teachings as disciples, forsaking all to follow Him, and the seriousness of teaching only His words.

54973.summary: The class explores the title 'Son of the Right Hand' for Jesus Christ, emphasizing His role as the heir of all things and the one who sits at God's right hand. It draws parallels between Saul of the Old Testament and Saul of the New Testament to illustrate the theme of weakness and God's strength, culminating in the idea that believers are also called to embody this principle through faith and discipleship.
